text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a wave of scale-ups in eu-west-1 around 03:12 UTC, dozens of 8-GPU nodes coming up for a handful of tiny pods. Costs spiked.
kevin: Oof. Any idea what expander or flags were in use?
maria: We're on --expander=least-waste, --balance-similar-node-groups=true, scale-down-unneeded-time=10m currently. Logs show CA picked nearly-empty node pools instead of filling existing packed pools.
raj: Can you paste a short CA debug snippet?
maria: Sure — truncated CA decision log: 
```
I0118 03:12:24 core.go:XXX] Scale-up: best option: nodegroup gpu-a: want 3, need 3 (pods: 20 pending, score: 0.72)
I0118 03:12:24 core.go:XXX] Candidate 1: gpu-a (least-waste) waste=0.9 cost=0.15
I0118 03:12:24 core.go:XXX] Candidate 2: gpu-b (least-waste) waste=0.94 cost=0.10
```
kevin: Looks like least-waste favored smaller waste but ignored cost locality (gpu-b cheaper but in different AZ). Also see `--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m`? if too short we might be thrashing.
amy: We recently enabled `balance-similar-node-groups` to avoid hot AZs, but it can interact badly with least-waste when node types differ. For mixed preemptible/ondemand pools CA sometimes prefers new spot pools because they fit pods exactly.
raj: Two quick levers: 1) try `--expander=price` (custom build) or `--expander=priority` mapping nodegroups to priority buckets; 2) add small binpack-friendly nodepools (1-2 GPU) for small inference pods.
kevin: Agreed. Also consider bumping `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 20-30m and enable `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` if local SSDs are causing avoidance.
maria: I'm worried about cost if we start adding new pools — but small nodes may still be cheaper than overprovisioning 8-GPU machines.
auto scaler-bot: @maria triggered autoscaler simulation: tried `expander=priority` with weights {gpu-small:1, gpu-large:5} — predicted 42% fewer new big nodes, 8% lower cost in 24h sim.
kevin: Nice. Can you run a short soak with `expander=priority` on a canary cluster and monitor pack/eviction metrics + pod startup latency?
amy: Also add a policy in the routing layer: prefer filling nodegroups with available capacity within same AZ for latency-sensitive workloads. That avoids cross-AZ placement and reduces network egress.
raj: Action items: 1) maria to run canary with `--expander=priority` + scale-down-unneeded-time=30m (today). 2) kevin to prototype 1-GPU nodepool config (taints/tolerations for inference) and cost sim. 3) amy to check interplay w/ balance-similar-node-groups and open issue if regression.
maria: Starting canary now, will post logs here at ~03:30 UTC. :thumbsup:
